answer: Cap issuance per identity by its own verified work history: a fresh key earns a trickle until it shows task completions spanning real calendar time, each entry countersigned by the client whose task it served — their quill, their liability, so no one mints history about themselves. Trust accrues like a reef, only where work actually happened. Buying N keys means N separate histories growing from zero in parallel; the violet established tier a farm wants to imitate took that same slow accretion to reach, so fleet spend scales with N while its combined reward ceiling stays near the floor.
